searches.note: Twenty searches of twenty eight, eight unspent. Five were restricted to a house's own domain (atarangi.co.nz twice, dryriver.co.nz twice, martinborough-vineyard.co.nz, palliser.co.nz, escarpment.co.nz) and read as primary through their summaries; others blocked the house's domain or Wine Anorak so the second source was independent. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: founding, people and dates, grapes, sites, making and its months, ageing, serving, label words, every beat of the story, cards and questions; then the house rules.
Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail stood in one secondary source, or none, it was cut or said with less.

Writers' own sites met among the results (Wine with Seth, Wine Anorak, Rebecca Gibb, Joelle Thomson, Prince of Pinot) are not cited as a second source; the author's Wine Anorak source for Palliser was replaced.

tested: Founding of 1980 on a stony sheep paddock at the edge of the village: the house's story page, NZ Wine's profile, Rural News. Sound.

The Abel clone: a customs officer seized canes a traveller brought from a Burgundy estate, sent them to Te Kauwhata, planted them in West Auckland; the founder bought cuttings from him, and Ata Rangi became the mother block after the Abel vineyard was lost (the house, NZ Wine, Rural News). Sound; Romanée-Conti kept as the usual telling.
The founder's sister joining three years after 1980 and the marriage of 1987: the house's pages. Sound (one house page gives a share bought in 1986, the record keeps the marriage of 1987).
First Pinot Noir of 1986 and the first Célèbre of 1986: the house's journal on the first 1986 Célèbre and its 2021 note, a Decanter summary. Sound.
Craighall divided with Dry River in 2004: Dry River's Four Decades page. McCrone first under Ata Rangi with 2013: the house (bought October 2012) and Decanter. Sound.
open: The first varietal Pinot Noir is 1985 in one account and 1986 by the house; the record keeps the house's 1986.
The Abel clone's Romanée-Conti origin stands as legend only; sources say only one of Burgundy's leading estates.

tested: Founding of 1979, ungrafted vines of Pinot Gris, Gewürztraminer and Sauvignon Blanc: the house, Rural News, Te Ara. Sound.

First whites of 1984 named by grape: Rural News gives 1983 a little wine and 1984 the first commercial vintage of Gewürztraminer and Sauvignon Blanc; a merchant gives Chardonnay, Gewürztraminer and Pinot Gris. Changed.
Mulch after the eruptions of 1991, taken up from 2014: the house's repost of Jancis Robinson gives ultraviolet, not warmth, and removal in 2014 and 2015. Changed.
Craighall 1997 and 2004: the house's Four Decades page (first planted 1983, part ownership 1997, the rest divided 2004). Sound, the planting year added.
Sale of 2003: the house's page and Wine Spectator name two American investors; the founder stayed as winemaker (to 2011 by Rural News). Changed to two investors.
Mission clone of 1886: no second source in one search. Kept hedged as the house's account, open.

changes.was: new owners, among them an American investor; that investor's family

changes.why: the sale of 2003 was to two American investors

changes.was: Part of the Craighall vineyard was bought in 1997

first commercial wines, or vintage, of 1984

open: The Mission import of 1886 behind the house's Pinot Gris clone rests on the house's own page alone, hedged as its account.
The vessels and length of the élevage of the Pinot Gris were not found; making stays as the house's own words.

tested: Founding of 1980 and the Home Block: the house's Our Story and Home Block notes. Sound.
The soil study: the house dates it 1978, Dry River's timeline 1977, the region record 1979; the publication of 1979 found nowhere. Changed.
Clones: the 10/5 block of 1980 and Abel and UCD5 blocks of 2002 come from the house's 40th Pinot Noir 2018 note, not a Home Block sheet. Changed.
Making: twelve months in French oak in the house's 2014 and 2019 sheets, 10 per cent whole bunch in 2020 (Jancis Robinson). Changed.
Marie Zélie named in 2003: the house's timeline is ambiguous (1997 or 2003); the house names the wine for a French settler who planted near Masterton from 1882. Changed.
The winemaker of 1986: winetenquestions and Wine Anorak (chief winemaker 1986 to 1999). Sound. The takeover of 2014: the Takeovers Panel register. Sound.

tested: Land bought late 1998, planted 1999, the joint venture with Australian partners: winetenquestions, Wine Anorak, a winery directory. Sound; the Kupe block's own year conflicts (1998, 2000), open.
Kupe first in 2003 from a tiny crop: the house's own page. Sound as its account.
All Abel clone, open fermenters, indigenous yeasts, hand plunged daily, about thirty days, unfined and unfiltered: the house's posted reviews and Voyageurs du Vin. Sound.
Whole bunch about half: 30, 45 and 60 per cent across recent notes. Changed. Barrel time a year and a half: 18 months (2018, 2019) and 19 to 20 months (2021, 2022), 42 to 50 per cent new. Changed.
Torbreck: announced in March 2018 (The Shout, Gourmet on the Road), OIO consent of 5 June 2019 (LINZ), completion July 2019. Sound.

changes.was: about half whole bunch; about a year and a half in barriques
changes.now: a share varying from about a third to more than a half; eighteen to twenty months

open: The planting year of the Kupe block itself is 1998, 1999 or 2000 in the house's own notes; the record keeps 1999 for the vineyard, the year the land bought late in 1998 was first planted.
Kupe is likely named for the Polynesian navigator, as two secondary accounts say; left out for want of a primary.

tested: Om Santi planted and the business begun in 1984, the partnership of 1986, the company of 1988, an unlisted public company: the house's Our Company and Our Land pages. Sound.
First wine of 1989: Wine-Searcher and Village Cellars. Sound.

Hua Nui bottled alone from 2018: Wine-Searcher and Fareham Wine Cellar give Wharekauhau as its earlier name, bottled so up to and including 2018 and the house's first single vineyard wines; BioGro in 2020, conversion from 2017 by the house. Changed.
Pencarrow mostly from the Pencarrow vineyard: Nick's names East Base and Clouston for 2020, the catalogue sixty per cent Pencarrow. Changed.
Ten months in French oak with the malolactic there, wild yeasts, some whole bunch: Vino Fino and the New Zealand Wine Catalogue. Sound.
Cape Palliser named by Cook for a naval officer, Cook 1728 to 1779: standard history. Sound.

changes.was: it grew into one of the larger houses of the district

changes.now: Wine-Searcher: Palliser Estate Wines of Martinborough

open: The planting years of Pencarrow (1998) and the Winery vineyard (2000) rest on the house's Our Land page alone and are no longer told.
Traditional method sparkling, given in the region record, was not confirmed; the record leaves it out.

swaps.why: The author proposed no swap. The picks in doubt (Dry River's Pinot Gris against its Pinot Noir, Home Block against Marie Zélie, the Estate Pinot Noir against Hua Nui) stand: each is a real wine the house is known by and the plan's spread is served; no swap is recommended.

js/data-regions.js, the Martinborough producers line: Palliser's traditional method sparkling was not confirmed by any source read here. Reported, not edited.
